about: What an existing install of Epic Cash Desktop / Epic Cash Mobile depends on. tools/check-install-contract.sh (in tools/check.sh) fails when the code drops a probe's text or when the items change without a change record. How to change an item: docs/install-contract.md.

items.what: Desktop data folder: everything (wallets, node, settings, logs, contacts, the Windows secret store) lives in <home>/.epic_cash_desktop (%USERPROFILE% on Windows, $HOME elsewhere).
Phone data folder: the app's private application-support folder (/data/user/0/<package>/files), from path_provider.
The first wallet's folder (Wallet 1, listed as legacy-<chain>). 26.10.24 renamed it to `wallet` without a migration: the incident this contract exists for.

probes.contains: static String firstWalletDir(String root, Chain chain) => '$root${_sep}wallets$_sep${chain.name}';
static String rootOf(String firstDir, Chain chain) => Directory(firstDir).parent.parent.path;

items.what: An added wallet's folder (desktop wallets 2..n), id = 32 hex characters.

probes.contains: static String walletDirOf(String root, Chain chain, String id) => '${_walletsIn(root, chain)}$_sep$id$_sep${chain.name}';

items.what: LEPIC's database inside a wallet folder: the app decides a wallet exists by this subfolder.

LEPIC's database files inside the lepic folder. 26.10.24-r2 and older keep the plain wallet.sqlite3 (+ -wal, -shm). From 26.10.25 the records are in the encrypted wallet.enc.sqlite3 with its key check wallet.enc.sqlite3.check; the first open copies the plain database into it, checks it and switches, then renames the plain one wallet.sqlite3.pre-encryption (+ -wal; -shm deleted), kept for one release. A plain wallet.sqlite3 an older build made after a rollback is set aside as wallet.sqlite3.after-rollback-<unix> and a restore scan runs.

The app's own per-wallet file beside LEPIC's database (notes, contacts, imported history, the old core's records). From 26.10.25 sealed by the wallet into wfe_meta.sealed beside it on unlock; wfe_meta.json stays in place, never written again, read as the migration source (merged in, adding only, when an older build changed it) until the release after 26.10.25 retires it.
The wallet list: file name, format version and the fields an older file holds; the first wallets' ids.
items.value: <data>/wallets.json {version: 1, lastUsedId, wallets: [{id, label, chain, dataDir, createdAt, ...}]}; first wallet id legacy-<chain>

items.what: The built-in node's folder, its per-chain subfolder and its toml (the chain data below is many GB: a rename means a full resync).
The user's settings file in the data folder and its keys (a renamed key reads as the default: the user's servers and switches are lost).
items.value: <data>/settings.toml: node.servers, epicbox.servers, online.status_site, online.update_check, online.price, local_node.api_port, local_node.p2p_port, network.mode

items.what: The one-time import of what 26.10.23 and older kept in the store into settings.toml, and its done-mark. Removing it loses the servers of every install that skipped 26.10.24/25.

The shared address book in the data folder. From 26.10.25 sealed into contacts.sealed under a random key that each wallet keeps sealed by itself in contacts.keys/<walletId>.key, with contacts.lock as the one-process lock; contacts.json stays in place, never written again, read as the migration source (merged in, adding only, when an older build changed it) until the release after 26.10.25 retires it.

The plain-http agreements for tailnet (CGNAT) nodes: settings.toml's [node] plain_http. 26.10.25 and older kept them in <data>/lan_nodes.json, read once at start and moved in (store mark app.lanNodesMoved), never written. Removing the reader before every install ran the move makes their tailnet node stop working.
items.value: settings.toml [node] plain_http; <data>/lan_nodes.json read once, + store key app.lanNodesMoved

items.what: The mark that first-run Setup finished (without it an installed wallet is sent through Setup again).
The log a user sends with a report.
History backups users keep (.wfeh): the extension and the payload version; every newer app opens every older file.
items.value: .wfeh, WFEH container version 1, payload version 2 (1 still opens)

items.what: Windows secret store: one DPAPI-sealed file in the data folder (the wallet's sealed password, the PIN vault, every app.* and desk.* key).

Linux secret store: the libsecret entry flutter_secure_storage_linux names after the application id (label <APPLICATION_ID>/FlutterSecureStorage, account <APPLICATION_ID>.secureStorage). Another application id is an empty store.
flutter_secure_storage pinned to an exact version with its options: plugin majors have migrated or dropped the Android/Linux storage format, and resetOnError must stay off.

The store keys of a wallet's sealed secrets: the pinned prefix per chain, the path prefix of a first wallet made before pinning (it contains the wallet folder's path: a folder rename orphans these too), and an added wallet's id prefix.
Desktop saved state in the store: settings, prefs, own nodes, favourites, the window, per-wallet records, remembered passwords.
items.value: desk.settings, desk.prefs, desk.nodes, desk.favourites[.<id>], desk.window, desk.wallet.<chain>[.<id>], desk.http[.<id>], desk.remember.<id>

items.what: App preferences in the store (both apps), and the updater's anti-rollback state (losing it lets an older signed manifest through).
items.value: app.theme, app.fiat, app.show_fiat, app.hide_balances, app.auto_lock, app.language, app.helpLanguage, app.advanced, app.advanced_prefs, app.payment_prefs, app.send_strategy, app.split_change, app.update_state

items.what: Android package name: another one installs as a separate app with an empty data folder and store.
The release signing certificate (SHA-256): Android refuses an update signed with another key. The key itself is outside every repository.
Inno Setup identity: AppId (a new GUID installs beside the old version), the per-user install folder, the exe name the uninstaller and updater find, and the single-instance mutexes Setup waits on.
The Linux executable name (AppImage and tarball users start it by name; the desktop updater replaces it).

Where 26.10.24+ apps look for the signed update manifest (update-v2.json). Each installed version keeps reading its own list for good, so these must keep serving; a new source is added, never swapped.
The prefix a 26.10.24+ app accepts download URLs under (the manifest's file URLs must start with it).

Installs up to 26.10.23 read the old-format update.json at the old addresses compiled into them, and accept downloads only under the old download folder. The publish tool keeps writing it; dropping it strands every such install on its version.
items.value: https://examples.btlabs.uk/epic-cash-wallets/update.json, update.json in the Pages repository (GitLab raw, GitHub Pages); downloads under https://examples.btlabs.uk/epic-cash-wallets/

items.what: The manifest's signed type and the BT Labs signing keys every installed app trusts (rank 1 signs, rank 2 retires it). A manifest typed otherwise or signed by another key is refused by every install.

not_frozen.note: Not frozen until the first signed Apple release (bundle ids are now uk.btlabs.epiccashwallet.macos / uk.btlabs.btwallet.ios, set 2026-10-30; the iOS id became uk.btlabs.btwallet.ios on 2026-11-02, before any App ID was registered). Freeze it then: bundle id, keychain service, data folder (<home>/.epic_cash_desktop, shared with the desktop item), Team ID.
Not frozen until the first signed Apple release. Freeze it then: bundle id, keychain access group, App Store id.

not_frozen.value: flutter_secure_storage, first_unlock_this_device, login keychain on macOS
not_frozen.note: Not frozen until the first signed Apple release: the keychain entries follow the bundle id and Team ID.

changes.change: First contract, from main 2221aa17, checked against 26.10.23 (v26.10.23), the last release before 26.10.24 renamed wallets/<chain> to wallet with no migration, and against b1c52350 (26.10.24-r2), which put the 26.10.23 names back.
changes.migration: None needed: every item is what 26.10.23 and 26.10.24-r2 already use. Store-to-settings.toml (26.10.23 kept servers in the store) is the import in all.settings_import_26_10_23. The 26.10.24 stray <data>/wallet folder is left alone and never read.

changes.change: updates.manifest_urls: the third source, https://btlabs-epic.github.io/update-v2.json (GitHub Pages of the BTLabs-EPIC organisation, dead since GitHub flagged that account), becomes https://github.com/BTLabsUK/wallet-for-epic/releases/latest/download/update-v2.json, the GitHub Release mirror of the new BTLabsUK organisation. The other two sources are unchanged.
changes.migration: None needed: app-config.toml ships read-only with each build, so installed apps keep their own list (BT Labs' server first, then the GitLab copy) and update exactly as before; only builds from this commit read the new source. Its answer is checked with the same keys and anti-rollback serial as every source, and a 404 (no GitHub Release yet) counts as no information, like the dead address did.
changes.approved_by: the owner, 2026-10-30 (this URL change, in the GitHub mirror job)

changes.change: desktop.lan_nodes_file becomes all.lan_nodes_file: the plain-http agreements for tailnet (CGNAT, 100.64/10) nodes move from <data>/lan_nodes.json into settings.toml's [node] plain_http, next to the node list, so hosts live only in settings.toml (docs/settings-file.md). The phone wrote the same file in its app folder, so Android is listed too.
changes.migration: Once at start, after the data folder is settled and settings.toml is open (importLanNodesFile in openAppSettings): each node of the Node list that lan_nodes.json agreed for (matched by host:port, 80 when none) joins [node] plain_http through the settings writer (comments, unknown keys and order kept; tmp file and rename); agreements for nodes no longer in the list are dropped. The store mark app.lanNodesMoved is written only after the file holds them; a rerun after a crash adds nothing the file has. lan_nodes.json is left as it was and never written again, so a rollback to 26.10.25 still finds it; its reader can be taken out one release after this ships. Installs without the file keep the first-run rule: tailnet nodes already in the list count as agreed when first used.
changes.approved_by: the owner, 2026-11-01 (explicit yes to this install-contract change, lan-nodes-merge job)

changes.change: Wallet records encrypted at rest. New item all.wallet_db_files: LEPIC's database moves from the plain <wallet folder>/lepic/wallet.sqlite3 to the encrypted wallet.enc.sqlite3 (SQLite3 Multiple Ciphers, ChaCha20-Poly1305, key from the seed) with its key check wallet.enc.sqlite3.check; the plain database is renamed wallet.sqlite3.pre-encryption, so an older build never resumes from a stale database (output keys the new build already used). all.wallet_meta_file and all.contacts_file gain the sealed files beside them (wfe_meta.sealed; contacts.sealed, contacts.keys/<walletId>.key, contacts.lock); wfe_meta.json and contacts.json stay where they are.
changes.migration: At the first unlock, under LEPIC's directory lock: the plain database is opened read-only (its schema never migrated before the switch), copied with its WAL into wallet.enc.sqlite3.tmp under the store key, checked (quick_check, user_version, row count of every table), the key check written, then tmp renamed to wallet.enc.sqlite3 (the switch), the plain file renamed wallet.sqlite3.pre-encryption and kept one release. Before the switch nothing outside tmp changes and a crash restarts the copy from scratch; after it a plain file beside a matching record only finishes the rename. A copy that fails (disk full) keeps the session on the plain file and tries again at the next open. Then the app seals wfe_meta.json into wfe_meta.sealed and contacts.json into contacts.sealed (each tmp, flushed, read back and opened, renamed), recording the plain file's size and hash; the plain files are left as they were, so a rollback to 26.10.24-r2 keeps notes and the address book, and a plain file an older build changed since is merged back in (adding only). After a rollback the older build's new plain database is set aside as wallet.sqlite3.after-rollback-<unix> and a restore scan runs. The shared book is used by one app process at a time (contacts.lock); a second one waits, then leaves it closed.
changes.approved_by: the owner, 2026-11-01 (explicit yes to this install-contract record: database renamed, app files kept)
